whatWasBuilt.classifier: packages/swing-lab/src/paddleMergeSafety.ts (merge-safety-v1): classifyMergeCandidate / enumerateMergeCandidatePairs / sweepMergeCandidates. Five checks per candidate fragment pair — segment-level ownership agreement (joint tail/head segments, tracker's otherOwnershipFactor both ways), target compatibility (each whole fragment against the tracker's own selection gates: maxMeanWristDistance 0.22 + minHandAffinity 0.4), event locality (bridged gap must not overlap eventPeak ± 300ms — the rally2 30→145ms mechanism: merged fragments fabricate paddle speed inside the contact window), motion continuity (forward AND backward constant-velocity corridors at 0.6× the reconciliation radius + velocity-cosine ≥ 0), non-target contradiction (sustained other-owned run ≥ 3 inside either fragment — the rally1 695ms mechanism: merged other-player fragment feeding target-gated contact). Verdict: any FAIL → MERGE_UNSAFE; all five PASS → MERGE_SAFE; otherwise UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN blocks merge exactly like MERGE_UNSAFE — absent evidence never upgrades a pair.
whatWasBuilt.provenance: Every report enumerates bridgedFrames with per-frame provenance: fragment frames OBSERVED; gap frames PREDICTED (constant-velocity, never observed) unless a measured target wrist lies within the hand-affinity radius (0.13) of the predicted position, then TRACKED. Estimates are never observations.

honestNegatives: The sweep carries zero wrist evidence, so ownership agreement, target compatibility and non-target contradiction were never exercised against real pose on real footage — only synthetically in unit tests. A Mac pass with canonical runs must repeat the sweep with real wrist series before any pair can ever be MERGE_SAFE in practice.

The 695ms/145ms numbers themselves were NOT reproduced here (they require the full cascade on canonical macOS runs); the classifier was validated against the committed detector artifacts and windows of those cases, not against regenerated cascade outputs.

MERGE_SAFE has never been observed on real data (9/9 real pairs UNSAFE); the positive control is synthetic. That is the intended bias — safety must be proven — but it means the classifier's permissive path is untested on footage.
